issue.title: "undefined reference" linker error with ARM build
issue.body:
I'm able to successfully build MAVSDK with the following cmake command

cmake -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-10 -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-latomic" -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF ..

But when I try to build a project that links against libmavsdk, I'm getting the following linker errors

/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_ldset4_acq_rel'
/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_ldadd8_acq_rel'
/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_cas4_acq_rel'
/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_ldadd2_acq_rel'
/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_swp4_acq_rel'
/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_ldadd4_acq_rel'
/usr/local/lib/libmavsdk.so.2.12.2: undefined reference to `__aarch64_swp1_acq_rel'

Ubuntu 18.04.6 LTS
g++-10 (Ubuntu 10.3.0-1ubuntu1~18.04~1) 10.3.0
cmake version 3.27.1

comments.body:
I changed the compiler to

set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER g++-10)

and most of the linker errors go away. Only one is being reported now.

/usr/bin/ld: ArduRoverControl: hidden symbol `__aarch64_ldset4_acq_rel' in /usr/lib/gcc/aarch64-linux-gnu/10/libgcc.a(ldset_4_4.o) is referenced by DSO

Did you mean to try to rebuild libmavsdk with "-mno-outline-atomics" or add the flag to the CMakeLists.txt file for the project I'm trying to build that links against libmavsdk? 

I tried to add the "-mno-outline-atomics" flag to my project that links against libmavsdk and I still get the "hidden symbol" linker error.
The linking error seems to happen in your own code ArduRoverControl? No?
Yes, the linking error is happening in my code. It is not happening when attempting to build libmavsdk. I'm able to successfully build/install libmavsdk.
Right, so it's not a libmavsdk issue?

I think so, I also tried the QuickStart guide:

https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/quickstart.html

And when I try to "sudo dpkg..." the .deb file I get the following error:

dpkg: error processing archive libmavsdk-dev_1.4.16_ubuntu20.04_amd64.deb (--install):
 package architecture (amd64) does not match system (arm64)
Errors were encountered while processing:
 libmavsdk-dev_1.4.16_ubuntu20.04_amd64.deb

Anyway, I noticed that there's a docker folder in the repo, but I can't find any docker build instructions. Is docker the preferred method for building libmavsdk for arm64? 

Update: I'm reading the README.md file in the docker folder, so I'm going to try to build with docker.

Looks like the run-docker script doesn't support arm64.

sudo ./run-docker-clang-format.sh
Unable to find image 'mavsdk/mavsdk-clang-format:latest' locally
latest: Pulling from mavsdk/mavsdk-clang-format
9c704ecd0c69: Pull complete 
06e936d8a7cd: Pull complete 
5f67a7f1391d: Pull complete 
Digest: sha256:8df530b2cd8340895063792cdd04cd0e53bc815b9f3b3189994a4436779a03ec
Status: Downloaded newer image for mavsdk/mavsdk-clang-format:latest
WARNING: The requested image's platform (linux/amd64) does not match the detected host platform (linux/arm64/v8) and no specific platform was requested
exec /bin/bash: exec format error
Why are you trying to install amd64 on arm?

thanks for catching that. I was just blindly using the example shell commands to install the pre-built library. 

Jetson Nano can support 32bit ARMv7 libraries, but the Ubuntu image Nvidia provides does not support 32bit libraries by default. I had to do this:

sudo dpkg --add-architecture armhf
sudo apt update
sudo apt install libc6:armhf

before I can install with this:

wget https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v2.12.5/libmavsdk-dev_2.12.5_debian12_armv7.deb
sudo dpkg -i libmavsdk-dev_2.12.5_debian12_armv7.deb

I also had to add some linker instructions to my CMakeLists.txt file to force the linker to use gcc_s instead of the static version. 

target_link_libraries(ArduRoverControl
    MAVSDK::mavsdk
    atomic
    gcc_s
)

set_target_properties(ArduRoverControl PROPERTIES
    LINK_FLAGS "-shared-libgcc -latomic -fuse-ld=gold"
)

I'm now able to successfully link libmavsdk!! 

Thanks for all the help.
BTW, I was assuming there isn't an ARMv8 prebuilt version of libmavsdk since I only saw arm6 and arm7 at https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases
